title: The new displays need a screen at least 1024px wide, otherwise List
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Work Orders page on the build under test, signed in with Work Orders view permission.
  2. A few work orders exist at the current location (create them via New Work Order if needed).
  3. You have a desktop browser whose window you can resize; a tablet is helpful but optional.
custom_steps:
1. Make the browser window narrower than 1024 pixels wide and open the Work Orders page.
  2. Read whether a display switcher (List / Tech View / Board View) is offered, and which layout shows.
  3. Widen the window to 1024 pixels or more and read whether Tech View and Board View become available.
  4. If a tablet is available, open the page on it held sideways (1024 pixels wide or more) and confirm the display options appear.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Below 1024px the Work Orders page shows List exactly as today (the phone card layout) with no display switcher.
  • At 1024px and wider, Tech View and Board View are offered on any device (a tablet at >=1024px gets them too); the switch is by screen width only and never detects the device type.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10044 — Switch between display options. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S1-R14 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R14: “The display options follow the same screen-width switch the List uses in production today. On a screen narrower than 1024px, the Work Orders page shows List exactly as it does today (the phone card layout), with no display switcher. At 1024px and wider, Tech View and Board View are offered, whatever the device: a tablet held sideways at 1024px or wider gets them too. The switch is by screen width only; the app never detects the device type.”
